ops.title: SECURITY: a socket squatter's signals reach the client before any trust verification
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.1 security re-review; present in shipped v0.20.x.

`wire.NewClient` dials, writes the hello, and reads the ack — `internal/wire/client.go:216-232`,
`internal/wire/hello.go:129-171` — all **before** `authorizeServer` runs at `control.go:137`.

So a same-UID process that unlinks and rebinds the daemon socket can, without passing any trust
check: forge `ErrDraining` (2 bytes) and pin any consumer in `WaitReady`'s retry loop indefinitely;
forge `ErrBuildMismatch` and drive a consumer into a redeploy; harvest the schema digest. None of
these requires surviving verification — verification simply happens too late.

This also subsumes the reacquire hole: with the gate inside `NewClient`, an attach that skipped it is
not constructible.

ops.text: wire.ClientConfig carries an Authorize hook invoked between dial and the hello write
A nil Authorize with a unix dialer is a config error, asserted by a test
A test proves a forged drain preamble and a forged reject ack are both refused before the hello write
The captured-conn closure at control.go:116-125 is deleted
